methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
REGENT Craft is a Series A transportation company founded by Billy Thalheimer and Mike Klinker that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of eight private frontier-transport peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero; no public comparables exist in this nascent category.

The stage-progression method is applicable and forms the sole quantitative anchor. Using the $60M total raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied value of $120M. The peer-median method is not applicable; while three same-sector peers exist, none meet narrow filters for stage, adjacency, or valuation tier, and a broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. The range reflects uncertainty in stage-progression multipliers rather than multi-method triangulation. Key risks include the thinness of the private transportation-tech peer set, the early stage of the sector, and the binary nature of frontier-tech value creation. Validation of assumptions around capital efficiency and path-to-revenue will be critical to post-Series A repricing.
